findings.observation: Reviewed Sheet 5 (General Notes Sheet) block-7.md. Found a section titled 'AUSTIN ENERGY STANDARD NOTES' containing 5 numbered notes. The first 4 notes align with the required standard notes from the reference material: (1) Tree pruning/easement rights note stating Austin Energy's right to prune trees and perform work in compliance with Chapter 25-8, Subchapter B; (2) Easement/access obligations note requiring owner/developer to provide easements for electric facilities; (3) Erosion control responsibilities note covering temporary erosion control, revegetation, tree protection, and tree pruning/removal within 10 feet of overhead electrical facilities; (4) NESC/OSHA clearance maintenance note detailing owner's responsibility for maintaining clearances per National Electric Safety Code and OSHA regulations near overhead power lines. A 5th note about relocation costs is also present but not part of the required 4 notes.
findings.reasoning: The grouping file requires 4 specific Austin Energy standard notes covering tree pruning rights, easement obligations, erosion control responsibilities, and NESC/OSHA clearance maintenance. All 4 required notes are present on Sheet 5 with substantive content that matches the template language at approximately 90% semantic threshold. The wording preserves the regulatory obligations and key references (Chapter 25-8, NESC, OSHA) while being formatted in all caps. The presence of an additional 5th note does not constitute a deficiency since the requirement is for the 4 specified notes to be present, not that only those 4 notes appear. The notes can appear on any sheet per the grouping guidance, and they are properly located on the General Notes Sheet.
findings.explanation: All 4 required Austin Energy standard notes present on Sheet 5 with ~90% semantic match to template language.

findings.observation: Used semantic search to identify sheets with existing electric facility legends and depictions. Found Sheet 8 (Existing Conditions & Demolition Plan 1 of 2) with legend defining symbols for existing overhead electric, existing power poles, existing light poles, existing guy anchors, existing electric meters, and existing electric manholes. Used vision tool to verify Sheet 8 showing: (1) Existing overhead electric lines running along Kinney Avenue and Collier Street; (2) Existing overhead electric line crossing diagonally through the property (marked for removal); (3) Existing underground electric line to residence (to be removed); (4) Abandoned underground electric line (to be removed); (5) Multiple existing power poles along perimeter; (6) Existing electric meter on residence; (7) Electric easements documented with doc numbers; (8) Guy anchors and light poles. Sheet 9 (Existing Conditions & Demolition Plan 2 of 2) also contains similar legend entries for existing electric facilities.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item requires existing electric utility facilities (both overhead and underground) to be shown on plan sheets. Sheet 8 comprehensively depicts existing electric infrastructure including overhead lines, underground lines, poles, meters, manholes, and easements. The legend clearly defines all electric-related symbols, and the vision analysis confirms these facilities are visually depicted on the plan with specific callouts and labels. Both overhead and underground facilities are shown, satisfying the requirement. The fact that many are marked for removal does not negate their depiction as existing facilities - the requirement is to show what exists, which has been done.
findings.explanation: Existing electric facilities (overhead lines, underground lines, poles, meters, manholes) shown on Sheets 8-9 with proper legend and callouts.

findings.observation: Used semantic search to identify sheets with proposed electric facility legends and depictions. Found Sheet 18 (Overall Utility Plan) with legend showing symbols for proposed underground electric, proposed transformers, proposed electric manholes, and proposed pull boxes. Used vision tool to verify Sheet 18 showing: (1) Proposed underground electric lines (UGE) running along southern and western site boundaries and branching toward the building; (2) Multiple callouts reading 'UNDERGROUND ELECTRIC LINE (SEE PLANS BY OTHERS)'; (3) Proposed transformer near northwest side of building with callout 'PROPOSED TRANSFORMER'; (4) Proposed electric manholes and 48-inch electric pull boxes along the underground electric routing; (5) Variable width electric clearance zones along the electric lines. Additional sheets (14, 17, 11) also contain legends with proposed electric symbols including proposed overhead electric lines, proposed electric poles, and proposed electric manholes.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item requires proposed electric utility facilities to be shown on plan sheets. Sheet 18 comprehensively depicts proposed electric infrastructure including underground electric lines with proper UGE designation, transformers, electric manholes, pull boxes, and clearance zones. The legend clearly defines all proposed electric symbols, and the vision analysis confirms these facilities are visually depicted with specific callouts. While the primary proposed infrastructure is underground (with reference to 'plans by others'), the requirement is satisfied by showing the proposed facilities on the site plan. The presence of legends on multiple sheets (14, 17) showing proposed overhead electric and poles suggests the full scope of proposed electric work is documented across the plan set.
findings.explanation: Proposed electric facilities (underground lines, transformers, manholes, pull boxes) shown on Sheet 18 with proper legend and callouts; additional proposed electric symbols in legends on Sheets 14, 17.

findings.observation: Reviewed facts.md to determine site zoning. The three parcels comprising the site are zoned: Tract 1 (3.44 ac) - CS-V-DB90 (Commercial Services, Vertical Mixed Use, Density Bonus 90); Tract 2 (0.16 ac) - CS-V-CO (Commercial Services, Vertical Mixed Use, Conditional Overlay); Tract 3 (1.61 ac) - CS-V-CO with marginal SF-3. None of the parcels are zoned CBD (Central Business District) or DMU (Downtown Mixed Use). The grouping file states the AEGB Letter of Intent is required only 'If zoned CBD or DMU' per LDC § 25-2-593(B). The condition is not met for this site.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item has a conditional trigger: it applies only if the site is zoned CBD or DMU. The facts clearly establish that all three tracts are zoned CS-V with various combining districts (DB90, CO) and no CBD or DMU zoning is present. The Key Terms section of the grouping file defines CBD/DMU as specific downtown base zoning districts that trigger the AEGB LOI requirement at the site plan stage. Since the site does not meet the zoning condition, this item is not applicable to this project. The site is using the Density Bonus 90 (DB90) affordable housing program, but that does not trigger the LOI requirement at site plan stage - only CBD/DMU zoning does per the cited regulation.
findings.explanation: Site is zoned CS-V-DB90, CS-V-CO, and CS-V-CO (with marginal SF-3); not zoned CBD or DMU, so AEGB Letter of Intent not required.

summary: 4 checklist items evaluated: 3 items pass (AE-01, AE-02, AE-03), 0 items fail, 1 item not-applicable (AEGB-02).
